title: Guardian trust closure — startup failure, terminal evidence, journal recovery, quiescence, execution slot release

KFF-B00-002.root_cause: A failed spawn emits `error` and `close` and never `exit`; terminal-evidence logic hung off the `exit` path, so no startup-failure closure was ever written, flushActionJournal could not release the command, and the agent_single_execution_slot stayed occupied across restarts.
fix: apps/agent/src/guardian.ts: one-shot `settle()` reached from `error` (only when child.pid === undefined), `exit` and `close`; startup-failure evidence written only when started/submitted/contextOpened are all false.
apps/agent/src/main.ts: flushJournal() now runs in `finally` even when the run rejects, so the closure written for a failed start actually releases the slot.
proof: journal phase stays `claimed` with no guardian_pid and no quarantined flag
closure on disk is kff.guardian-closure-startup-failed.v1 with context_opened:false and no context_closed
wire endpoints for the failed command are exactly ['commands/<id>/status','commands/<id>/quiescence'] — zero /submit, zero /context-opened, zero platform write
DB: command DONE with quiesced_at, action CANCELED/GUARDIAN_STARTUP_FAILED, one attempt, one action.reported, one guardian.quiesced
SELECT count(*) FROM kff.agent_commands WHERE agent_id=$1 AND state IN ('READY','CLAIMED') === 0

KFF-B00-004.requirement: Tests must truly enter the production Guardian startup-failure path and prove the target branch was hit, not merely construct a similar object, test helper, mocked return value, or observe exit code 0.
how: tests/unit/guardian-termination.test.ts drives the real runGuardian against a real child process; the fault is a real libuv ENOENT produced by pointing process.cwd() at a path that does not exist, which is exactly the production spawn call site (spawn(process.execPath, ..., { cwd: process.cwd() })).

tests/integration/guardian-recovery.test.ts launches the real apps/agent/src/main.ts from a copy of the node binary and renames that copy away, turning the agent's own spawn into a real ENOENT, then restores it for the next command.
Branch-hit evidence is the closure protocol version on disk, the journal phase/guardian_pid pair, and the exact set of controller endpoints reached.

KFF-B00-003.reason: It sits directly on the Guardian closure / compactClosure / quiescence trust chain.
KFF-B00-003.principle_applied: 'never opened a context' and 'opened one and later proved it closed' are two different facts; compaction may shorten evidence but must not change its meaning.
fix: new protocol version kff.guardian-closure-startup-failed.v1 carrying context_opened: literal(false) and deliberately no context_closed
compactClosure now refuses anything that is not kff.guardian-closure.v1, so a startup-failed or already-compact record is returned untouched
closureProof keeps the originating version, so a startup failure can never be read back as a closed context and every proof already on record stays byte-identical
recordQuiescence projects browser_status='CLOSED' only for kff.guardian-closure.v1
KFF-B00-003.real_path_proof: In the integration run the retention pass really executed compactClosure over the startup-failure entry (collection_redaction.reason === 'DELIVERED') and the record on disk still carried the startup-failed version with context_opened:false and no context_closed.

red.observed_error: Error { "code": "ENOENT" } propagated raw out of runGuardian instead of GUARDIAN_STARTUP_FAILED
red.note: C / D / E were already green on the old code by design: they assert behaviour that must not change.

command_1.scenario: deliberate pre-start spawn failure (real libuv ENOENT inside runGuardian)

command_2.scenario: independent legal command, queued only after the slot came back

stability_sample.honest_note: The residual failure is KFF-B01-NEW-01. It did not reproduce after clearing orphaned guardian processes and 34 leftover temp roots. This does NOT prove it is gone. No failure was masked by retrying.

idempotency_and_race.error_only: NOT_OBSERVED — a failed spawn always emits error then close
idempotency_and_race.error_then_close: OBSERVED — exactly one terminal decision; a second would surface as IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT and as a second closure file (unit scenario B)
idempotency_and_race.error_then_exit: NOT_OBSERVED — the only error sources are a failed spawn (no exit) and a failed IPC send, and the production send path both checks child.connected and always passes a callback, which is where the failure is delivered (unit scenario F pins both halves with a real probe)
idempotency_and_race.double_callback_duplicate_event: OBSERVED as error+close; settled flag guarantees one decision
idempotency_and_race.agent_restart_during_recovery: OBSERVED (integration test 2): the restarted agent re-sends the same event_id, kff.inbound_events absorbs it as duplicate with no side effects, and the same proof is resumed
idempotency_and_race.repeated_flush: OBSERVED at unit and integration level: a second flush over a settled entry performs no work; exactly one action.reported and one guardian.quiesced
idempotency_and_race.double_slot_release: none observed — quiesced_at is COALESCE-guarded and the audit event is digest-guarded
idempotency_and_race.deliberately_not_fabricated: Combinations this platform does not produce were recorded as NOT_OBSERVED with the reason, not turned into synthetic platform facts.

new_findings.title: A guardian child that is spawned, sends ready, receives start and then stalls produces no terminal event at all
new_findings.symptom: Same user-visible failure as KFF-B00-002 through a different trigger: runGuardian's promise never settles, main.ts finally never runs, flushActionJournal never runs, the command stays CLAIMED with quiesced_at NULL and no closure, and the agent's main loop blocks inside await runGuardian. A restart does not self-heal.
evidence: journal entries {phase:'claimed', guardian_pid:15388} and {phase:'claimed', guardian_pid:17248} with no closure file
profile directory WAS created (binding.json, owner.lock, user-data/Default)
controller seen log shows only repeated heartbeats after the claim — no /status, no /action-reports, no /quiescence
DB row state CLAIMED with quiesced_at NULL
two detached node-copy.exe guardian-child processes survived their parent on Windows
new_findings.hang_site: packages/adapters/src/browser-inbox.ts calls hooks.onContext(managed.context) unconditionally after openManagedBrowser, and the journal phase was still `claimed`, so the child hung inside openManagedBrowser — i.e. in chromium.launchPersistentContext(userData, {..., timeout: 20000}) or before it.
new_findings.observed_rate: 2 in ~30 runs (~10%) in the prior session; 0 in 11 runs this session after clearing orphaned processes and leftover temp roots. Not reproduced is not fixed.
why_not_fixed_in_b01: Phase 8 forbids creating a second Guardian state machine, journal or bypass recovery scheduler
a parent-side no-progress deadline would fire on legitimately long browser work unless the child reports progress, which is a protocol extension the planner must decide
an unprovable case must keep GUARDIAN_UNCONFIRMED / quarantine semantics rather than fabricate closure
new_findings.self_diagnosing_test: tests/integration/guardian-recovery.test.ts waitForProof() now prints journal.phase, journal.guardian_pid, controller.state and controller.quiesced_at on timeout instead of failing with a bare timeout.

unknown_paths_remaining: A child that dies after `start` keeps GUARDIAN_UNCONFIRMED and its isolation by design — this is correct behaviour, covered by unit scenarios D and E
A startup-failure record paired with an action already in SUBMITTING is rewritten to UNKNOWN_OUTCOME at unit level; unreachable in production because a startup failure always precedes PREPARING
error + exit is NOT_OBSERVED on this platform, with the reason captured by a real probe (unit scenario F)

final_answers.recommend_entering_B02: yes, after the planner rules on KFF-B01-NEW-01
